children: IREN shares (IREN) edged higher in early morning trading on Wednesday after the company said it is betting on European companies that want to run their artificial intelligence (AI) closer to home. The AI cloud provider said it plans to offer managed AI cloud services from a planned campus in Badajoz, Spain, with initial operations targeted for 2028.
, adding it had set up IREN Europe, a holding company for its business in the region, and had obtained the civil works license for the Spanish site, which the firm originally announced in May.

was up over 4% in pre-market trading, erasing its previous-day loss. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around IREN remained in the ‘extremely bullish’ zone, accompanied by ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.
IREN Targets Europe’s Sovereign AI Demand
Sovereign AI means local control of data and compute. Customers in Europe care about “where their data sits and who’s running the infrastructure,” said Co-CEO Daniel Roberts.

IREN intends to merge the Badajoz capacity with Mirantis' software, which it purchased earlier this year. That includes Mirantis’ k0rdent AI platform, which can deploy and manage AI infrastructure while keeping customer workloads separate, the company said. It also allows customers to choose where data is stored and how it is secured, IREN said. According to an earlier release from the company, IREN announced Aug. 4 that it had closed the deal with Mirantis.

The campus is expected to have about 300 megawatts (MW) of capacity, IREN said. The company has already secured grid power for the site. It said it continues to hold close discussions with local, regional and national authorities as the project develops.
The company stated the site will use closed-loop liquid cooling, which uses very little water. IREN is also making the site compatible to work with NVIDIA’s DSX AI Factory Platform.

IREN took ownership of Badajoz through its acquisition of Spanish developer Nostrum Group. The deal closed in June and added about 490MW of secured power in Spain, and its team of more than 60 is led by Gabriel Nebreda, Chief Executive Officer of IREN Spain.

Former Banco Santander CEO Ángel Corcóstegui will chair the board of IREN Europe, the company said. Roberto Purcaro, previously head of Complex Opportunities globally at Macquarie Capital, has joined the board as Executive Director for the Europe division.

Purcaro said “Badajoz is where IREN Europe begins,” adding that “IREN develops its own sites and operates them directly and will do the same in Europe.” He added that “Our focus from here is the campus and the customers who’ll use it.”
No customers were identified for Badajoz in the release. The 2028 start date is also still a target subject to permits, grid connections, and financing, IREN said.
IREN has been down over 29% so far this year, and lost over 55% in the last 12 months.
IREN shares surged over 4% in premarket trading Wednesday after the AI cloud provider said it plans to offer managed AI cloud services from a planned campus in Badajoz, Spain.
The company made the announcement during its GTC Berlin conference and also launched IREN Europe.
Demand for sovereign AI services is growing as European customers grow more concerned about where their data is stored, Co-CEO Daniel Roberts said.

title: IREN Stock Rises: AI Cloud Provider Plans 300MW AI Campus In Spain For 2028
